claim: For every integer \(n\ge2\), define the singleton fingerprint of a Bernoulli product by \(F_i(\mathbf p)=p_i\prod_{j\ne i}(1-p_j)\) on \(\mathbf p\in[0,1)^n\). Then \(F\) is injective on \(\{\mathbf p:\sum_i p_i\le1\}\). Consequently, for every \(0\le\lambda<1\), its restriction to \([0,\lambda]^n\) is injective if and only if \(\lambda\le1/n\). At the boundary \(\lambda=1/n\), there is no finite constant \(C\) such that \(\operatorname{TV}(\operatorname{Ber}(\mathbf p),\operatorname{Ber}(\mathbf q))\le C\|F(\mathbf p)-F(\mathbf q)\|_1\) for all \(\mathbf p,\mathbf q\in[0,1/n]^n\). For every \(\lambda>1/n\), distinct homogeneous parameter vectors in \([0,\lambda]^n\) can have exactly the same singleton fingerprint, so singleton-slice discrepancy cannot control total variation at all beyond that threshold.
integrity: The proof is self-contained and analytic. A supplementary deterministic verifier checks the homogeneous fold and boundary scaling but is not used as a substitute for proof. Full text of both highly relevant preprints was inspected; targeted research-index and literature searches found no statement implying the exact trichotomy, while an alias risk is retained.
scientific_limitations: The theorem gives the exact injectivity and stability barrier for the labeled singleton fingerprint. It does not prove a positive dimension-free total-variation comparison on the full region \(0\le\lambda<1/n\), and it does not address coarser unlabeled one-success statistics.
title: Sharp identifiability boundary for singleton slices of Bernoulli products
